Auditable Arbitration for Resolution

When an answer is not wrong, but the reason is gone.

A2R measures and reduces source-resolution distortion in LLM output arbitration: the irreversible loss or incorrect mapping of task-relevant source structure when several candidate answers become one.

01 / About

Arbitration is a compression problem.

LLM-as-a-Judge systems often produce a plausible final answer by merging, rewriting, or selecting among candidate outputs. Plausibility alone does not tell us whether the relationships that supported the answer survived.

A2R fixes a query-conditioned reference structure before arbitration, then asks whether source units, conflicts, provenance, caveats, and local relations remain recoverable in the final output.

A correct-looking sentence can still erase a conflict, detach a caveat, or misattribute a claim.

02 / Method

A sparse ledger before a fluent answer.

A2R-Decision makes the local resolution state explicit before final generation. The ordering matters: extract first, resolve second, render last.

Stage 1E

Unit extraction

Read the query and candidates, then preserve query-relevant claims, conditions, caveats, evidence, and recommendations as source units.

source ID · span · attributes
Stage 2L

Decision ledger

Record the relation between units and the operation it licenses: merge, condition, drop, or report unresolved.

relation · operation · provenance
Stage 3G

Tagged rendering

Serialize ledger claims with deterministic ordering, caveat scope, and source-aware tags. No extra free rewriting is required.

organize · render · attach tags
(q, A, B)→Û→L̂→ŷ extract · ledger · generate
03 / Evidence

Preference is not recoverability.

Two answers can be similarly preferred while differing sharply in whether a reader can reconstruct the source-side decision.

The framework separates primary fidelity metrics from safety diagnostics and mechanism analysis.

CERconflict erasure
FCRfalse conflict
UARunsupported addition
Prov-Hprovenance recoverability
CPRcaveat preservation
RF*relation fidelity
Final-only fidelity↓ lower is better · ↑ higher is better
SystemCER ↓Prov-H ↑

Main-set comparison across 520 pairwise cases. A2R-Decision improves both conflict preservation and provenance recoverability at 1.44× Checklist Prompt token cost.

05 / Dataset

A benchmark for source-bounded arbitration.

The benchmark fixes gold source structures before system execution, so evaluation can focus on what arbitration preserved, erased, or mapped incorrectly.

Open dataset
320controlled diagnostic cases
200natural pairwise cases
150query-contrast groups
200three-candidate checks

The released artifacts exclude annotator identities, raw annotator logs, account metadata, and identifying free-text notes.
